title: audit-and-stage-sdk-minor-upgrades-with-sidecar-shims
creator: Aisha Moreno
description:
Problem: Language SDKs for Python/JS/Go have accumulated minor version drift across transport, HTTP clients, and utility libs. Multiple support shims exist to preserve old API shapes and test harnesses reference pinned transitive deps. This makes CI slow, increases image sizes, and blocks runtime performance improvements that require newer client libraries.

Goal: Produce a safe, auditable plan to bump a prioritized set of minor dependencies across the three language clients, validate parity of behavior, and remove or replace compatibility shims with a lightweight sidecar adapter where needed. The work should be staged so we can roll forward quickly while preserving stability for existing customers.

Scope: Audit current direct and critical transitive deps for the three official SDKs (python-client, js-client, go-client), prepare a compatibility matrix, stage upgrade PRs in small grouped batches (network/transport, serialization, auth), add temporary sidecar shims for any behavioral changes, and create rollout/runbook for canary + full rollout.

Out-of-scope: Major library rewrites, breaking API surface changes, or migrating to a different transport protocol (e.g., HTTP->gRPC) are not part of this ticket and will be handled in follow-up epics.
acceptance_criteria: Complete dependency audit spreadsheet with versions, licensing, and risk notes for python/js/go
Open grouped PRs per language with minimal diffs and passing CI and unit tests
Sidecar shims implemented and covered by integration tests for any behavioral regressions
Measure and confirm no >5% increase in median latency in SDK microbenchmarks and <2% increase in package size (or document rationale)
Rollout plan documented with canary criteria and automated rollback steps
tasks: Inventory current direct and transitive dependencies (week 1)
Prioritize candidate upgrades and create compatibility matrix (week 1)
Implement transport/HTTP client minor bumps in python-client (PR: python/dep-bump-1)
Implement transport minor bumps in js-client (PR: js/dep-bump-1)
Implement transport minor bumps in go-client (PR: go/dep-bump-1)
Add sidecar adapter abstraction and feature-flag it for canary users
Add integration tests exercising auth/serialization/edge cases
Run microbenchmarks and package-size checks, document results
Stage canary rollout and monitor errors/latency for 48h
Merge and coordinate release notes and changelog entries

2026-03-02 - Liam Chen: Assigned; started inventory job and forked repo targets. Identified three risky transitive deps: httpx (python), node-fetch (js), golang.org/x/net (go).
2026-03-04 - Priya Kapoor (review): Suggest grouping by transport vs serialization to minimize blast radius. Also requested benchmarks for each PR.
2026-03-06 - Liam Chen: Implemented initial python-client bump for httpx 0.24 -> 0.25 behind feature flag. Unit tests pass locally; CI flaky on macOS runners (investigating).

2026-03-08 - Designated QA (Marco Silva): Added integration test matrix for serializer versions and edge-case payloads. Found 1 behavior change in JS JSON reviver when bumping a dependency; working with js lead to add shim.

notes: Risk mitigation: if a minor bump causes observable customer-facing differences we will toggle calls through the sidecar adapter and ship a rollback path that pins the transitive dep for the SDK build. Aim to keep each PR small (<5 files changed) and group by logical layer to reduce review overhead. Coordinate with release engineering for package publishing windows.
